title: Saidu Sharif I Stupa
subtitle: Buddhist stupa on the edge of Saidu Sharif, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Saidu Sharif I Stupa and Monastery

edits: A bench up to 24 m wide is cut along the jeep track to the smoothed track profile (the 30 m DSM includes tree canopy).
Road bumps and ruts in the drive are illustrative; the grade and the line of the track are real.
Trees, shrubs, grass tufts and boulders are placed where WorldCover maps that cover; their size and number are illustrative.
The walking loop is a 150 m circle around the arrival point; it is not a mapped trail.

The main stupa is the Atlas maquette (backend/tools/blender/stupa.py): the square base 19.6 m x 3.2 m, the first cylindrical body (tier) 13.4 m and the drum 13.1 m are measured from the MAIP restitution drawing's scale bar; only the surviving base is modelled, and its stair faces north as Wikipedia describes. The model is placed by the build at the ground of the place point.
The lower terrace (the Terrace of the Stupas) is levelled to the ground at the place point out to 30 m and paved in grey schist; the 30 m radius is estimated, no source gives the terrace's size.
The low dressed-stone edge of the terrace (about 0.9 m high) is estimated from photo 3; its height and line are not surveyed.
Eight minor stupas on square bases, on a ring 22 m from the main stupa, are estimated from photos 1 and 2; their number, positions and sizes are illustrative, not measured.

The four corner columns with crouching lions on the top of the square base are restored, not surviving: Wikipedia says the four columns stood on the corners, and their heights (about 9 m shafts, lions to about 17 m) are estimated from the MAIP restitution drawing's scale bar.

The monastery on the upper terrace is drawn inside the OSM footprint 'Saidu Sharif Monastery' (way 1078000527) as a walled courtyard, 24 m by 38 m, with six cells along each long side: cell sizes, wall heights and flat roofs are estimated. Its ground is the DEM, which is not levelled to a separate upper terrace (no source gives that height); the 30 m DEM cannot show the cut.
Ground under the monastery and the town follows the real DEM slope; the cells sit on it and are not levelled.

The walking circle is a 36 m circle around the stupa terrace; it is not a mapped trail. The walk from the trailhead on Saidu Sharif Road to the stupa crosses the town ground on the easiest slope over the DEM.
The walk from the end of the jeep track follows the mapped OSM footpath for 0.0 km; the last 0.39 km is not mapped and is traced over the ground (easiest slope on the DEM).
The 1167 buildings stand on their OSM footprints; their height (OSM levels where mapped, else one or two storeys), roofs and colours are illustrative, after visitors' photos.
Season colours, snow, ice and dawn mist are illustrative.

Traffic on the drive is illustrative: the vehicle kinds are those seen on Swat roads (Willys jeeps, Hilux, Suzuki vans, Mehran cars, CD70 motorbikes, Qingqi rickshaws, painted trucks); their number and movement are not counted.
